problem: 'the test is done at constant other variable' is vague: a student may not see which variable is held fixed, and the phrase adds nothing because a partial derivative is already defined at constant other variable.
fix: Write: '∂M/∂y is taken holding x constant, and ∂N/∂x is taken holding y constant.'

problem: The work is taken as the area under each P–V path without saying the paths are quasi-static. Area under the curve equals work only when the gas pressure is defined at every step and equals the plotted pressure. Exam trap 4 correctly warns that ∫P dV fails for an irreversible sudden expansion, so the example as written can look inconsistent with the trap.
fix: Add at the start: 'Both paths are quasi-static, so the gas pressure is defined at every point and the area under the path equals the work done by the gas.'

problem: The first-law sign convention is never stated in the text, yet the Q4 answer uses ΔU = Q − W with W taken as work done by the system. A student using the opposite convention (work done on the system) gets Q_B − Q_A = −3 J.
fix: State once in the text: 'Work done by the system is positive here, so the first law is ΔU = Q − W.'

problem: 'the first law ties the difference to the path' is ambiguous. The first law makes Q − W = ΔU the same for all paths, so the difference between Q and W does not depend on the path; only Q and W separately do.
fix: Write: 'the first law gives Q − W = ΔU for every path, so a path needing more work also needs more heat; Q and W change with the path, but their difference does not.'

fix: Replace with links such as 1.3, using the correct chapter ids.
